--- license: cc-by-4.0 language: - he pipeline_tag: automatic-speech-recognition base_model: Zengwei/icefall-asr-librispeech-streaming-zipformer-2023-05-17 tags: - speech - asr - hebrew - streaming - zipformer - transducer - icefall - k2 --- # zipformer2-66m-streaming-he > **Developed by Yakov Kolani.** This is a mirror of his original model, > [thewh1teagle/zipformer2-66m-streaming-he](https://huggingface.co/thewh1teagle/zipformer2-66m-streaming-he) > (CC-BY-4.0), with additional ONNX exports for browsers and GPUs in [`onnx/`](#additional-onnx-exports-onnx). > Used by [live-transcribe.ivrit.ai](https://live-transcribe.ivrit.ai) for on-device transcription. Streaming Hebrew speech recognition: a 66 M-parameter Zipformer2 transducer, fine-tuned from [icefall's English streaming Zipformer](https://huggingface.co/Zengwei/icefall-asr-librispeech-streaming-zipformer-2023-05-17) on [ivrit.ai](https://www.ivrit.ai) Hebrew audio. Decodes in 1.28 s chunks as audio arrives. ## Usage (sherpa-onnx) ```sh uv pip install sherpa-onnx soundfile numpy huggingface_hub uv run hf download thewh1teagle/zipformer2-66m-streaming-he --include "sherpa-onnx/*" --local-dir . ``` ```python import numpy as np, sherpa_onnx, soundfile as sf model_dir = "sherpa-onnx" recognizer = sherpa_onnx.OnlineRecognizer.from_transducer( tokens=f"{model_dir}/tokens.txt", encoder=f"{model_dir}/encoder.int8.onnx", decoder=f"{model_dir}/decoder.int8.onnx", joiner=f"{model_dir}/joiner.int8.onnx", model_type="zipformer2", num_threads=4, ) audio, sample_rate = sf.read("audio.wav", dtype="float32", always_2d=True) stream = recognizer.create_stream() stream.accept_waveform(sample_rate, audio.mean(axis=1)) stream.accept_waveform(sample_rate, np.zeros(int(1.5 * sample_rate), dtype=np.float32)) # flush the last chunk stream.input_finished() while recognizer.is_ready(stream): recognizer.decode_stream(stream) print(recognizer.get_result(stream)) ```
PyTorch checkpoint (icefall) `model.pt` holds an [icefall](https://github.com/k2-fsa/icefall) Zipformer2 `AsrModel` state dict under `"model"`, the config under `"config"` and the SentencePiece tokenizer under `"tokenizer"` (same as `bpe.model`). | Setting | Value | |---|---| | `num_encoder_layers` | 2,2,3,4,3,2 | | `downsampling_factor` | 1,2,4,8,4,2 | | `feedforward_dim` | 512,768,1024,1536,1024,768 | | `num_heads` | 4,4,4,8,4,4 | | `encoder_dim` | 192,256,384,512,384,256 | | `encoder_unmasked_dim` | 192,192,256,256,256,192 | | `cnn_module_kernel` | 31,31,15,15,15,31 | | `query_head_dim` / `value_head_dim` / `pos_head_dim` / `pos_dim` | 32 / 12 / 4 / 48 | | `decoder_dim` / `joiner_dim` / `context_size` | 512 / 512 / 2 | | `vocab_size` (blank = 0) | 1493 | | `causal` | true; chunk 64 (1.28 s), left context 256 frames | | Features | 80-dim fbank, 16 kHz mono |
## Results WER (%, lower is better) on ivrit.ai's test sets with the [leaderboard](https://huggingface.co/spaces/ivrit-ai/hebrew-transcription-leaderboard) normalization. Other numbers are from the leaderboard; all are offline (full-utterance) except where marked. | Model | eval-d1 ↓ | eval-whatsapp ↓ | |---|---|---| | Soniox | 4.8 | 9.0 | | **🌊 zipformer2-66m-streaming-he (this model)** | **5.1** | **8.9** | | ivrit-ai/whisper-large-v3-turbo | 5.3 | 7.1 | | parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-he | 6.1 | 8.8 | | openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo | 8.4 | 12.8 | | NVIDIA nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b (streaming) | 17.1 | 36.5 | The sherpa-onnx int8 export scores 5.3 / 8.8. ## Additional ONNX exports (`onnx/`) Added by ivrit.ai to Yakov Kolani's model. The original repo ships only the int8 sherpa-onnx export; these are full-precision exports of the same `model.pt`, with identical inputs and outputs (drop-in for sherpa-onnx or onnxruntime). | File | Notes | |---|---| | `encoder.onnx`, `decoder.onnx`, `joiner.onnx` | fp32, icefall `zipformer/export-onnx-streaming.py`, chunk 64 (1.28 s), left context 256 | | `encoder.fp16.onnx`, `decoder.fp16.onnx`, `joiner.fp16.onnx` | fp16 weights and compute, fp32 inputs/outputs (for WebGPU / CUDA). Encoder output vs fp32: min cosine 0.99999 over a streamed utterance | | `config.json` | Chunking parameters and every encoder state tensor (name, shape, dtype) for runtimes that need to initialize streaming state themselves, e.g. onnxruntime-web | | `tokens.txt` | Same as `sherpa-onnx/tokens.txt` | On 15 eval-whatsapp clips, int8 (`sherpa-onnx/`) and fp32 scored 9.31% and 9.40% WER, so int8 loses nothing measurable. In the browser (onnxruntime-web 1.30), the int8 export on the WASM backend was about as fast as fp16 on WebGPU on an integrated GPU, at half the download, so live-transcribe.ivrit.ai uses int8 + WASM. ## Limitations - English is weak (spelled letter by letter). - Numbers come out as words or digits inconsistently. ## Fine-tuning & training notes
Fine-tune this model Load `model.pt["model"]` into icefall's Zipformer2 `AsrModel` (config above) and continue with icefall's `finetune.py` or any transducer training loop. - Audio 16 kHz mono; normalize text like training: strip nikud and bidi marks, geresh/gershayim → `'`/`"`. - ScaledAdam `base_lr 0.0045`, Eden `lr_batches 7500` / `lr_epochs 2`, ~600 s of audio per step.
How it was trained (new language on an English streaming Zipformer) - **Extend the tokenizer, don't replace it.** A 1,024-piece Hebrew SentencePiece model, trained on ~500 h of transcripts, appended after the English 500 pieces (1,493 total). New embedding and output rows start at the mean of the old rows (+1% noise). - **10× LR on decoder + joiner**, so the new rows separate quickly. - **Let the LR decay.** icefall's `finetune.py` defaults (`lr_batches 100000` / `lr_epochs 100`) keep the LR flat, which stalled a new language at ~20% WER; `lr_batches 7500` / `lr_epochs 2` fixed it. - **Data:** ~20k h of ivrit.ai audio pseudo-labeled with ivrit.ai Whisper models. Drop labels the teacher cut off at its token cap (they teach deletions) and `compression_ratio > 2.6` (Whisper loops). Rows sharing word 8-grams with the eval sets were removed (no test leakage). - **Finish:** weight EMA, then the joiner's blank bias lowered by 1.0 (fewer dropped words, baked into the weights).

# pocket-tts-onnx

[Kyutai's Pocket TTS](https://github.com/kyutai-labs/pocket-tts) exported to ONNX for
[pocket-tts-onnx](https://github.com/thewh1teagle/pocket-tts-onnx), including a Hebrew IPA
adapter. Runs in the browser on onnxruntime-web, or in Python with onnxruntime and numpy.

**Try it:** https://thewh1teagle.github.io/pocket-tts-onnx/

## Web asset set

The browser app fetches these; they are hosted here rather than in a GitHub release because
release assets are not served with CORS headers.

| file | size | what |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `model.onnx` | 177 MB | the streaming step graph, int8, adapter bundled |
| `encoder.onnx` | 39 MB | the mimi voice encoder, fetched only when cloning |
| `assets.json` | 1.4 MB | config, tokenizer and voice conditionings |
| `manifest.json` | tiny | what to fetch and how big it is |
| `renikud.onnx` | 21 MB | Hebrew G2P, mirrored from [thewh1teagle/renikud](https://huggingface.co/thewh1teagle/renikud) |

## Single-file models

For the Python package, where everything rides inside one file:

| file | size |
| --- | --- |
| `pocket-tts-english.onnx` | 228 MB |
| `pocket-tts-english-ipa.onnx` | 231 MB |

```python
from pocket_tts_onnx import PocketTTS

tts = PocketTTS("pocket-tts-english-ipa.onnx")
samples, sample_rate = tts.create("Hello world.", voice="alba")
```

Voices baked in: `alba`, `cosette`, `javert`, `male1`.

# Piper Hebrew — noa (medium)

A [Piper](https://github.com/OHF-Voice/piper1-gpl) voice for Hebrew: **noa**, a natural female voice, plus an English
speaker (**ljspeech**) in the same model. Fast, CPU-friendly, standard Piper ONNX.

Type plain Hebrew — phonemes follow [renikud](https://renikud.github.io) (stressed IPA).

## Files

| File | |
|---|---|
| `he_IL-noa-medium.onnx` | Piper voice (ONNX, 22.05 kHz) |
| `he_IL-noa-medium.onnx.json` | Piper config (`phoneme_type: hebrew`, speakers) |
| `noa-ljspeech-step20322.pt` | PyTorch checkpoint (generator + discriminator) for further fine-tuning |

## Speakers

| Speaker | Id | Language |
|---|---|---|
| `noa` | 0 (default) | Hebrew |
| `ljspeech` | 1 | English |

## Usage

```sh
echo "הוא צפה בסרט וראה חיה שצפה במים." \
  | uvx --from piper-tts piper -m he_IL-noa-medium.onnx -f noa.wav
```

`phoneme_type` is `hebrew`: Piper converts plain Hebrew to stressed IPA with
[renikud](https://renikud.github.io), the phoneme convention this model is trained on.

## Training

- **Architecture** — Piper VITS, medium.
- **Init** — `en_US-ljspeech-medium` (trained from scratch on public-domain LJSpeech), converted to multi-speaker
  with the speaker conditioning zero-initialized.
- **Data**
  - **noa** — 24 h of Hebrew speech generated with [Chatterbox](https://github.com/resemble-ai/chatterbox),
    Knesset sentences, Whisper-filtered.
  - **ljspeech** — [LJSpeech](https://keithito.com/LJ-Speech-Dataset/) (public domain), ~24 h.
- **Steps** — 20,322 (best held-out mel L1 0.405).
- **Code** — [piper-tts-finetune](https://github.com/thewh1teagle/piper-tts-finetune).

# renikud

Hebrew grapheme-to-phoneme (G2P) model. Converts unvocalized Hebrew text to IPA phonemes.

- 85.1% word accuracy on [heb-g2p-benchmark](https://github.com/thewh1teagle/heb-g2p-benchmark)
- Single `.onnx` file, no extra dependencies
- Punctuation-conditional: preserves punctuation when present

## Usage

```python
from renikud_onnx import G2P

g2p = G2P("model.onnx")
print(g2p.phonemize("שלום עולם"))
# → ʃalˈom ʔolˈam
```

## Training

See [thewh1teagle/renikud](https://github.com/thewh1teagle/renikud) for the full training code.
